identity.name: Kingdom of Champasak
native_names: ນະຄອນຈຳປາສັກ

land.text: the southern part of Lan Xang that seceded in 1713

predecessors.note: Infobox predecessor: Kingdom of Lan Xang. 'The Kingdom of Champassak was founded in 1713 when the southern part of the Lan Xang seceded.' Cliopatria's row begins in 1709.

land.text: the south, which 'seceded during the following years' after the 1707 partition

predecessors.note: Kingdom of Vientiane page: 'The kingdoms of Champasak and Muang Phuan also seceded during the following years'; no year, no leader. The Cliopatria shapes of Champasak and Vientiane 1709 share no cell, so the 1709-1712 land has no owner in Cliopatria.

land.text: the Left Bank of the Mekong, which Cliopatria's French Indochina outline of 1895 covers wholly (129 of 129 cells of the 1890 Champasak outline)

successors.note: 'Following the Franco-Siamese crisis of 1893, the Left Bank fell under French rule as an administrative block' (Kingdom of Champasak page); the treaty is dated 3 October 1893 (Franco-Siamese crisis page). Cliopatria keeps the Champasak shape to 1894 and starts its French Indochina outline here in 1895. The kingdom's capital was 'transferred to French rule' in 1904 and the royal house continued to 1946 (page): not drawn.

capitals.name: Bassac (Champasak)
capitals.note: The page names Bassac and Champasak as the capital without dates, and its infobox gives Pakse without dates; 'In 1904, prior to the Franco-Siamese Treaty, the kingdom's capital was transferred to French rule'. Champasak town lies in the strip that Cliopatria removes in 1828.

rulers.name: Nokasad
rulers.note: Page list; the page does not describe the founding role.

rulers.name: Sayakumane
rulers.note: Taken by the Siamese in 1778; 'In 1780, King Sayakumane was allowed to return to Champasak as vassal to the Siamese king.'

rulers.name: Nho
rulers.note: Probably the 'Nyo' of the Lao rebellion page, Anouvong's son appointed king of Champasak, who 'led an estimated 2,000 men from Champasak to Ubon' in 1827; the page list spells the name Nho and gives no 1826 change.

rulers.name: Kham Souk
rulers.note: Reigned 1863-1899 (page list); cut at this dossier's 1893 end (reviewer se-01-h).

keyframe_review.note: Years only: applies 1713-1774. 42,010 km2 (147 cells), the south of Laos around Pakse with a corner of Cambodia and Vietnam. 'The Kingdom of Champassak was founded in 1713 when the southern part of the Lan Xang seceded' (Kingdom of Champasak page; the Vientiane page gives no year); Cliopatria begins in 1709. The page gives no area and no territory, so no infobox check. For 1709-1712 the land has no state in this dossier.
1775-1777: 42,066 km2, 55 km2 more than 1709 (one cell at the margin). No event on the page; King Taksin sent an army to Vientiane and Champasak 'in 1777'.

correction.text: shape unchanged; Siamese dependency from 1778 (military rule 1778-1779, vassal king from 1780), carried by the suzerain's vassal events

keyframe_review.note: 1778-1787: 42,010 km2. Status only: 'Champasak were made a dependency of Siam in 1778' and the infobox has 'Independent (1713-1778) Vassal of Siam (1778-1904)'; 'In 1779, the Siamese withdrew from the kingdoms of Vientiane and Champasak, leaving them under temporary military rule' (Lao rebellion page) and in 1780 Sayakumane returned 'as vassal to the Siamese king'. The land does not change.
1788-1790: 42,071 km2, a cell more than 1778; no event on the page.
1791-1795: 42,010 km2; no territorial event on the page. Fay Na 'appointed by Siam' in 1791.
1796-1827: 42,150 km2, the largest outline, a row of margin cells in the north; no event on the page. Anouvong's rebellion of 1826-1828 involved a Champasak force under Chao Nyo (Lao rebellion page).

Unverified: page silent. 1828-1884: 36,862 km2, the 1827 outline without 18 cells on the west bank around Champasak town (bbox 105.28-105.92 E, 14.11-15.34 N; 17 cells in Laos, 1 in Cambodia). The rebellion ended in 1828 ('Territorial changes: Siam consolidates control over Vientiane and Champasak'); the Kingdom of Champasak page has '1829-1893 Siam annexes Champassak following the Chao Anouvong Rebellion' and 'Champassak lost jurisdiction over the province of Stung Treng' (undated), and says 'The kingdom's capital was transferred to French rule' in 1904. No page dates or places the loss, so the shape stands and the ledger records a loss at confidence 1.
1885-1889: 36,637 km2, within a cell of 1828; no event on the page.

correction.text: shape unchanged; applies 1890-1893, to the treaty of 3 October 1893

keyframe_review.note: Years only: applies 1890-1893. 36,637 km2 (129 cells), all of it inside Cliopatria's French Indochina outline of 1895. The Franco-Siamese Treaty of 3 October 1893 ended the crisis ('Land on east bank of the Mekong ceded to Cambodia and Laos'); the Champasak page: 'the Left Bank fell under French rule as an administrative block'. Cliopatria keeps the Champasak shape to 1894 and starts French Indochina here in 1895, so 1894 is a gap in Cliopatria; the page does not mention Champasak.

region.text: the southern part of the Lan Xang

ledger.note: 1713: the Kingdom of Champasak secedes from Lan Xang. 'The Kingdom of Champassak was founded in 1713 when the southern part of the Lan Xang seceded.' Cliopatria draws it from 1709.

1778: the Siamese take Champasak. 'In 1777, King Taksin of Siam sent an invading army to the Kingdom of Vientiane and Champasak'; 'Champasak were made a dependency of Siam in 1778, joining Luang Prabang and Vientiane.' Hatched until the Siamese withdrawal; the Vientiane page names Phraya Chakri (the later Rama I) as the general.

1779: the Siamese withdraw. 'In 1779, the Siamese withdrew from the kingdoms of Vientiane and Champasak, leaving them under temporary military rule'; in 1780 King Sayakumane was allowed to return 'as vassal to the Siamese king' (Kingdom of Champasak page). The vassal tint is the suzerain's.

region.text: Ubon, where the Champasak force under Nyo marched

ledger.note: January 1827: the Lao armies march. 'In January 1827 the Lao armies of the kingdoms of Vientiane and Champasak moved south and west across the Khorat Plateau'; 'King Nyo also led an estimated 2,000 men from Champasak to Ubon' (Anouvong's rebellion of 1826-1828).
1828: the rebellion ends in a Siamese victory (infobox 'Date 1826-1828', 'Siamese victory'; 'Siam consolidates control over Vientiane and Champasak'). The page gives no month.

region.text: the 18 cells that Cliopatria's outline loses in 1828, on the west bank around Champasak town (17 in Laos, 1 in Cambodia)

ledger.note: 1828: Cliopatria removes the land around Champasak town. Page silent on the territory: the rebellion's infobox has 'Siam consolidates control over Vientiane and Champasak' and the Champasak page '1829-1893 Siam annexes Champassak following the Chao Anouvong Rebellion'. The strip is the 18 cells that Cliopatria's outline loses in 1828; the 1904 transfer of the capital to French rule is a later page-dated event.

region.text: the Left Bank of the Mekong, the whole Cliopatria outline

ledger.note: October 1893: the Left Bank passes to France. 'Following the Franco-Siamese crisis of 1893, the Left Bank fell under French rule as an administrative block'; the Franco-Siamese Treaty was signed on 3 October 1893 and the Siamese 'agreed to cede Laos to France' (crisis page, which does not name Champasak). The kingdom's capital and house stay under Siamese, then French, overlordship to 1904 and 1946 (not drawn).

wars.name: Siamese conquest of Vientiane and Champasak
wars.outcome: Siamese victory: Champasak became a dependency of Siam in 1778; the Siamese withdrew in 1779 leaving temporary military rule and Sayakumane returned as vassal in 1780. Vientiane was sacked in 1779.
wars.note: 'In 1777, King Taksin of Siam sent an invading army to the Kingdom of Vientiane and Champasak'. The Vientiane page dates the sack of Vientiane to 1779 and says nothing of a Siamese conquest of Champasak.

wars.name: Lao rebellion (1826–1828)
wars.outcome: Siamese victory: Vientiane abolished and 'The kingdoms of Champasak and Lan Na were drawn more closely into the Siamese administrative system.'
wars.note: Chao Nyo (Anouvong's son, king of Champasak) led about 2,000 men from Champasak to Ubon in 1827; the Kingdom of Champasak page dates the Siamese annexation 1829 (and says Suwannaphum, a different place, lost its status afterwards).

wars.name: Franco-Siamese crisis of 1893
wars.outcome: French victory: the Franco-Siamese Treaty of 3 October 1893 ceded the Left Bank of the Mekong to France; a 25-kilometre zone on the west bank was demilitarised.
wars.note: The page does not mention Champasak; the Champasak page puts the Left Bank under French rule after the crisis.

certainty.note: The page gives no frontiers for the kingdom; the Cliopatria outline of the Mekong, the Dangrek and the Annamite uplands is approximate. Cambodian, Vietnamese and Annamite claims (Stung Treng, Kontum, Pleiku) are undated.
The treaty of 3 October 1893 fixed the Mekong as the line; the dossier ends in the same month.

notes:
Cliopatria row 'Kingdom of Champasak' (1709-1894, 9 shapes), all reviewed. The Wikipedia field in Cliopatria and the seed is 'Champasak', a disambiguation page; the article is 'Kingdom of Champasak' and the identity uses it.
Dates: the pages give 1713 for the founding (Cliopatria 1709) and October 1893 for the loss of the Left Bank (Cliopatria 1894). The kingdom itself lasted to 1946 as a vassal of Siam (1778-1904) and then a French principality; only the Left Bank outline is drawn, so the dossier ends with it. Between 1709 and 1712 the land has no state: Cliopatria's Champasak and Vientiane shapes of 1709 share no cell and the pages give no year for the secession from Vientiane (vientiane dossier of another batch may claim it). In 1894 Cliopatria has no French Indochina outline over the Left Bank (it starts in 1895): french-indochina (se-03) should start the Left Bank in October 1893.
Counterparts needed from other batches: thonburi-kingdom (Siamese vassal tint for Champasak from 1778, and the Vientiane sack of 1779), rattanakosin-kingdom (vassalage, the 1828 gain and the 1829 'annexation'), vientiane (Cliopatria 1709-1827; the 1713 secession), french-indochina.
Conflicts and silences: the Kingdom of Champasak page says '1829-1893 Siam annexes Champassak' yet lists kings continuously (Huy 1828-1840 to Kham Souk 1863-1899), so annexation means loss of status, not of the dynasty; the Vientiane page has a Burmese vassalage 1765-1779 for Vientiane only. Undated: Champasak 'lost jurisdiction over the province of Stung Treng'; Kontum and Pleiku ceded to French Annam (page, undated). Cliopatria's shape holds 6 cells in Vietnam and 3 in Cambodia (Kontum, Pleiku and the Stung Treng side) throughout, not corrected. Cliopatria's 1828 outline loses the west-bank land around Champasak town; the page gives neither date nor taker (recorded at confidence 1). The brief's mention of Soi Sisamut and Phraya Supho is not on these pages. No page gives an area, so the area check could not be made.
Page budget: 5 pages of 5 (the first, the disambiguation page, was empty).
